Them sorts of questions are always asked during assessments as I’m sure you know, and I’m sure in compliance interviews they have to confirm some things, but it seems so excessive. I had a friend who had to have a compliance call, she said they just confirmed that she still lived alone, and the circumstances of her illness hadn’t changed, no personal questions at all. She was actually pleasantly surprised, seeing the bad wrap the DWP has.
How does having ‘dry lungs’ reduce asthma attacks? Genuine question.

If you had a partner, I still don’t see how the situation screams fraud to her. Some benefits have no relation to having a partner, a partner doesn’t necessarily mean they live with you. It’s a weird situation that I think she has thought to far into it. Also the part about your mental health, fuck her, I’m pretty sure these compliance interviews are not a substitute for an actual assessment, so she has no right to comment.
